paragraphs: Swamiji once ran into a man back home whom he remembered as extremely dull. He knew nothing, wanted to know nothing, and lived almost like an animal, without any spark of interest in anything.
This man asked Swamiji what he should do to know God and become free. Swamiji asked him whether he could tell a lie. The man said he could not.

Then, said Swamiji, he had better learn. Being able to lie was better than living like a beast or a block of wood. He had clearly not reached the highest state, which is beyond action and perfectly calm; he was simply inactive, too sluggish even to do something wrong.

Swamiji admitted this was an extreme example and that he had been joking. But his point was serious. A person has to become active first, and only by passing through activity can he reach true calmness.
learn: Laziness can masquerade as peace, but real calm comes after effort, not instead of it. If you feel stuck, start doing something, anything worthwhile: energy can be guided, but nothing can be built on inertia.
